summary: Only specially trained bank officials operate video KYC and check liveness; the bank's V-CIP application itself must also have face liveness / spoof detection (¶27(1)(v))
quote: The V-CIP process shall be operated only by officials of the bank specially trained for this purpose.
source: Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks – Know Your Customer) Directions, 2025 (RBI/DOR/2025-26/169, 28 Nov 2025, updated as on 1 Oct 2026)

summary: Any prompting at the customer end means the account opening is rejected
quote: The bank shall reject the account opening process if it observes any prompting at the customer end.
source: Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks – Know Your Customer) Directions, 2025 (RBI/DOR/2025-26/169, 28 Nov 2025, updated as on 1 Oct 2026)

summary: Banks may use AI to make video KYC robust
quote: The bank may use appropriate artificial intelligence (AI) technology to ensure that the V-CIP is robust.
source: Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks – Know Your Customer) Directions, 2025 (RBI/DOR/2025-26/169, 28 Nov 2025, updated as on 1 Oct 2026)

summary: Assisted video KYC through a Business Correspondent at the customer end
quote: The bank shall permit assisted V-CIP when it takes help of Business Correspondents (BCs) to facilitate the process only at the customer end.
source: Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks – Know Your Customer) Directions, 2025 (RBI/DOR/2025-26/169, 28 Nov 2025, updated as on 1 Oct 2026)

summary: Blinking, smiling or frowning is not mandatory for liveness
quote: Making specific facial gestures, like blinking of eyes, smiling, frowning, etc. is not mandatory for liveness check. The bank shall take due cognizance of special needs, if any, of the customer during liveness check.
source: Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks – Know Your Customer) Directions, 2025 (RBI/DOR/2025-26/169, 28 Nov 2025, updated as on 1 Oct 2026)

summary: Liveness checks must not exclude people with special needs
quote: The liveness check shall not result in exclusion of person with special needs.
source: Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks – Know Your Customer) Directions, 2025 (RBI/DOR/2025-26/169, 28 Nov 2025, updated as on 1 Oct 2026)

summary: No rejection without application of mind; reasons recorded; PwDs not denied
quote: The bank shall not reject an application for onboarding or periodic updation of KYC without application of mind. The officer concerned shall duly record the reason(s) for rejection.
source: Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks – Know Your Customer) Directions, 2025 (RBI/DOR/2025-26/169, 28 Nov 2025, updated as on 1 Oct 2026)

summary: KYC templates to capture disability type for accessible services
quote: KYC templates must capture disability type and percentage for providing accessible services.
source: Pragya Prasun v. Union of India, 2025 INSC 599 (30 Apr 2025)

summary: Customer signs or gives a thumb impression on the printed CAF in Digital KYC (the Supreme Court, ¶18(vi), separately directs acceptance of an image of a thumb impression)
quote: take a print of CAF, get signatures / thumb-impression of customer at appropriate place
source: Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks – Know Your Customer) Directions, 2025 (RBI/DOR/2025-26/169, 28 Nov 2025, updated as on 1 Oct 2026)

summary: Sign language, captions and audio descriptions
quote: provide sign language, captions and audio descriptions for visually and hearing-impaired users
source: Pragya Prasun v. Union of India, 2025 INSC 599 (30 Apr 2025)

summary: Aadhaar is not mandatory for KYC, except for people seeking a benefit or subsidy under section 7 of the Aadhaar Act
quote: Aadhaar number is not mandatory for purposes of KYC. However, in case the customer is desirous of receiving any benefit or subsidy under any scheme notified under section 7… the customer shall provide the Aadhaar number to the bank. In other cases, customers may provide the Aadhaar number voluntarily.
source: Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks – Know Your Customer) Directions, 2025 (RBI/DOR/2025-26/169, 28 Nov 2025, updated as on 1 Oct 2026)

summary: Aadhaar number must be redacted where not needed
quote: ensure that such customer redacts or blacks out his Aadhaar number
source: Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks – Know Your Customer) Directions, 2025 (RBI/DOR/2025-26/169, 28 Nov 2025, updated as on 1 Oct 2026)

summary: Offline Aadhaar XML/QR at most three working days old for video KYC
quote: the XML file or QR code generation date is not older than three working days from the date of carrying out V-CIP
source: Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks – Know Your Customer) Directions, 2025 (RBI/DOR/2025-26/169, 28 Nov 2025, updated as on 1 Oct 2026)

summary: Clear PAN image; printed copies of e-documents are not valid
quote: The use of printed copy of equivalent e-document, including an e-PAN is not valid for the V-CIP.
source: Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks – Know Your Customer) Directions, 2025 (RBI/DOR/2025-26/169, 28 Nov 2025, updated as on 1 Oct 2026)

summary: Digital KYC photo standards the bank's officer must meet; Sahay borrows them as guidance for customer-side photos
quote: The authorised officer shall ensure there is no skew or tilt in the mobile device while capturing the live photograph of the original documents… in proper light so that they are clearly readable and identifiable
source: Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks – Know Your Customer) Directions, 2025 (RBI/DOR/2025-26/169, 28 Nov 2025, updated as on 1 Oct 2026)

summary: Small Account with limits, valid 12 months (extendable by 12); signature or thumb impression certified by an officer
quote: the aggregate of all credits in a financial year does not exceed Rupees One Lakh… withdrawals and transfers in a month does not exceed ₹10,000… balance at any point of time does not exceed ₹50,000
source: Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks – Know Your Customer) Directions, 2025 (RBI/DOR/2025-26/169, 28 Nov 2025, updated as on 1 Oct 2026)

summary: Consent recorded in an auditable, alteration-proof way
quote: The bank shall record the customer consent in an auditable and alteration-proof manner.
source: Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks – Know Your Customer) Directions, 2025 (RBI/DOR/2025-26/169, 28 Nov 2025, updated as on 1 Oct 2026)

summary: Specific consent for Aadhaar OTP authentication
quote: The Customer shall give specific consent for the authentication through OTP.
source: Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks – Know Your Customer) Directions, 2025 (RBI/DOR/2025-26/169, 28 Nov 2025, updated as on 1 Oct 2026)

summary: Bank houses V-CIP infrastructure in its own premises; in a cloud deployment the data is the bank's and the cloud or third-party provider retains no data
quote: the cloud service provider or third-party technology provider assisting the V-CIP shall retain no data
source: Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks – Know Your Customer) Directions, 2025 (RBI/DOR/2025-26/169, 28 Nov 2025, updated as on 1 Oct 2026)

summary: Aadhaar Face Authentication by official, BC or business facilitator
quote: A bank official, business correspondent, or business facilitator can perform biometric-based e-KYC authentication, including Aadhaar Face Authentication.
source: Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks – Know Your Customer) Directions, 2025 (RBI/DOR/2025-26/169, 28 Nov 2025, updated as on 1 Oct 2026)

summary: Aadhaar OTP e-KYC with limits until full due diligence (term loans only, up to ₹60,000 a year)
quote: aggregate balance… shall not exceed Rupees One Lakh… aggregate of all credits in a financial year… shall not exceed Rupees Two Lakh… not… operate for more than one year unless it carries out identification
source: Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks – Know Your Customer) Directions, 2025 (RBI/DOR/2025-26/169, 28 Nov 2025, updated as on 1 Oct 2026)

summary: Offline Aadhaar verification
quote: proof of possession of Aadhaar under clause (2) above where offline verification can be carried out, the bank shall carry out offline verification
source: Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks – Know Your Customer) Directions, 2025 (RBI/DOR/2025-26/169, 28 Nov 2025, updated as on 1 Oct 2026)

summary: Video KYC (V-CIP) for new individual customers
quote: The bank may undertake V-CIP to carry out… CDD in case of new customer onboarding for individual customers
source: Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks – Know Your Customer) Directions, 2025 (RBI/DOR/2025-26/169, 28 Nov 2025, updated as on 1 Oct 2026)

summary: OTP as signature on the electronic CAF in Digital KYC, including a family member's mobile; the printed CAF is still signed or thumb-impressed (¶24(13))
quote: if the customer does not have their own mobile number, the bank may use the mobile number of their family / relatives / known persons for this purpose and clearly mention it in the CAF
source: Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks – Know Your Customer) Directions, 2025 (RBI/DOR/2025-26/169, 28 Nov 2025, updated as on 1 Oct 2026)

summary: Signature or ink thumb impression on the form
quote: certifies under their signature that the person opening the account has affixed their signature or thumb impression in their presence
source: Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks – Know Your Customer) Directions, 2025 (RBI/DOR/2025-26/169, 28 Nov 2025, updated as on 1 Oct 2026)

summary: Self-declaration through a BC (no change, or address change only) after biometric e-KYC; physical form allowed only until the bank offers the electronic mode
quote: after successful biometric based e-KYC authentication. Until the bank makes an option available in the electronic mode, the customer may submit such declaration in physical form.
source: Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks – Know Your Customer) Directions, 2025 (RBI/DOR/2025-26/169, 28 Nov 2025, updated as on 1 Oct 2026)

summary: Exception handling for subsidy seekers when e-KYC fails
quote: owing to injury, illness or infirmity on account of old age or otherwise… perform identification preferably by carrying out offline verification or alternatively by obtaining the certified copy of any other OVD
source: Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks – Know Your Customer) Directions, 2025 (RBI/DOR/2025-26/169, 28 Nov 2025, updated as on 1 Oct 2026)

summary: Digital KYC: customer visits the official, or the official visits the customer
quote: The customer, for the purpose of KYC, shall visit the location of the authorised official of the bank or vice-versa.
source: Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks – Know Your Customer) Directions, 2025 (RBI/DOR/2025-26/169, 28 Nov 2025, updated as on 1 Oct 2026)

summary: KYC Identifier with explicit consent to download records from CKYCR
quote: the KYC Identifier with an explicit consent to download records from CKYCR
source: Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks – Know Your Customer) Directions, 2025 (RBI/DOR/2025-26/169, 28 Nov 2025, updated as on 1 Oct 2026)

summary: Officially Valid Documents
quote: passport, the driving licence, proof of possession of Aadhaar number, the Voter's Identity Card…, the job card that NREGA issues…, and the letter that the National Population Register issues
source: Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks – Know Your Customer) Directions, 2025 (RBI/DOR/2025-26/169, 28 Nov 2025, updated as on 1 Oct 2026)

summary: PAN, its e-document, or Form No. 60
quote: PAN or the equivalent e-document thereof or Form No. 60 as defined in Income-tax Rules, 1962
source: Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks – Know Your Customer) Directions, 2025 (RBI/DOR/2025-26/169, 28 Nov 2025, updated as on 1 Oct 2026)

citation: RBI caution on KYC frauds (2 Feb 2024) · modus operandi
summary: How KYC frauds work: unsolicited calls, SMS or email; asking for personal or login details or to install unverified apps through links; false urgency and threats to freeze or close the account
quote: The modus operandi for such frauds usually involves customers receiving unsolicited communications…
source: RBI Press Release 2023-2024/1794, 'RBI cautions against frauds in the name of KYC updation' (2 Feb 2024)

citation: RBI caution on KYC frauds (2 Feb 2024) · Don'ts
summary: Never share login details, card details, PIN, password or OTP
quote: Do not share account login credentials, card information, PINs, passwords, OTPs with anyone.
source: RBI Press Release 2023-2024/1794, 'RBI cautions against frauds in the name of KYC updation' (2 Feb 2024)

citation: RBI caution on KYC frauds (2 Feb 2024) · Don'ts
summary: Do not click suspicious or unverified links
quote: Do not click on suspicious or unverified links received in mobile or email.
source: RBI Press Release 2023-2024/1794, 'RBI cautions against frauds in the name of KYC updation' (2 Feb 2024)

citation: RBI caution on KYC frauds (2 Feb 2024) · Don'ts
summary: Do not share sensitive information through unverified websites or apps
quote: Do not share any sensitive data/ information through unverified/unauthorized websites or applications.
source: RBI Press Release 2023-2024/1794, 'RBI cautions against frauds in the name of KYC updation' (2 Feb 2024)

citation: RBI caution on KYC frauds (2 Feb 2024) · Don'ts
summary: Do not share KYC documents with unknown people or organisations
quote: Do not share KYC documents or copies of KYC documents with unknown or unidentified individuals or organizations.
source: RBI Press Release 2023-2024/1794, 'RBI cautions against frauds in the name of KYC updation' (2 Feb 2024)

citation: RBI caution on KYC frauds (2 Feb 2024) · Do's
summary: Confirm any KYC request directly with the bank, using contact details from its official website
quote: directly contact their bank/ financial institution for confirmation/ assistance… only through its official website/ sources
source: RBI Press Release 2023-2024/1794, 'RBI cautions against frauds in the name of KYC updation' (2 Feb 2024)

citation: RBI caution on KYC frauds (2 Feb 2024) · reporting
summary: Report financial cyber fraud at once: National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal (cybercrime.gov.in) or helpline 1930
quote: In case of financial cyber frauds, members of public should immediately lodge a complaint…
source: RBI Press Release 2023-2024/1794, 'RBI cautions against frauds in the name of KYC updation' (2 Feb 2024)
